successors.note: The Taranto page: 'Tarentum surrendered to Rome after the death of Pyrrhus in Peloponnese in 272 BC.' The Magna Graecia timeline: '282-272 BC: Taranto was conquered by the Romans despite the intervention of Pyrrhus'.

correction.text: Taras and its territory (40 km disc round Taranto, 3,035 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Taras. Neither page gives the territory ('Chora or territory of ancient Taras: not described'); the infobox 249.86 km2 is the modern comune. The 40 km disc round Taranto (3,035 km2) is a reading. Taras's daughter colony Heraclea (433-432, with Thurii) was independent.

region.text: Taras and its territory (40 km disc round Taranto, 3,035 km2)

ledger.note: 706: Spartans found Taras. 'Taranto was founded in 706 BC by Dorian Greek immigrants hailing from Sparta'; the founders were the Partheniae ('sons of virgins'); Magna Graecia gives 'c. 706 BC, mother city Sparta, founders Phalanthos and the Partheniai'.

region.text: Taras and its territory (40 km disc round Taranto, 3,035 km2)

ledger.note: 272: Tarentum surrenders to Rome. 'Tarentum surrendered to Rome after the death of Pyrrhus in Peloponnese in 272 BC'; Magna Graecia: '282-272 BC: Taranto was conquered by the Romans despite the intervention of Pyrrhus'. Kingdom of Epirus's ledger has Tarentum under Epirote dominion from 280.

wars.name: Pyrrhic War

zones.text: Taras and its territory (40 km disc round Taranto, 3,035 km2)

wars.outcome: Pyrrhus helped Taranto against Rome and 'lost the battle of Beneventum in 275 BC'; Tarentum surrendered to Rome in 272.
wars.note: The Taranto page describes the war under 'Politics and military'; the Magna Graecia timeline gives Rome's war on Taranto as 282-272.

certainty.note: No page gives any frontier of Taras's territory.

sources.title: Taranto
sources.note: Founding 706 by Spartan Partheniae, Archytas first half of the 4th century, Cleonymus 303, Pyrrhus, Beneventum 275, surrender 272; silent on territory.

sources.title: Magna Graecia
sources.note: Founding table (Taras c. 706), colonies of Taras (Heraclea), Rome 272, timeline 282-272.

notes: Thin by page: Taranto and Magna Graecia date only the foundation (706) and the surrender (272) and say nothing of Taras's territory. Not on the pages: the 473 defeat by the Iapygians, Alexander of Epirus's help (334), the Italiote League, the socii navales treaty. Archytas ('the dominant figure in Tarentum in the first half of the 4th century', strategos seven years in a row) and Cleonymus (303) are not territorial. The disc is a reading of the chora. Gazetteer names used: Taranto (place, resolves).
